views.name: cards_base_projection
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  uuid,
  name,
  asciiName,
  artist,
  setCode,
  number,
  rarity,
  type,
  types,
  subtypes,
  supertypes,
  manaCost,
  convertedManaCost,
  faceConvertedManaCost,
  colors,
  colorIdentity,
  colorIndicator,
  availability,
  borderColor,
  layout,
  frameVersion,
  text,
  originalText,
  flavorText,
  power,
  toughness,
  loyalty,
  edhrecRank,
  isReprint,
  isPromo,
  isOnlineOnly,
  hasFoil,
  hasNonFoil,
  isFullArt,
  isAlternative,

  mtgoId,
  mtgoFoilId,
  multiverseId,
  mcmId,
  cardKingdomId,
  purchaseUrls,
  printings
FROM cards

params.description: A normalized, one-row-per-card projection of the cards table exposing identifying, descriptive, and collectible attributes for each card (grain = id).
params.when_to_use: Lookup detailed card attributes by card id or uuid | Filter cards by setCode, name, rarity, type, colors, or other card-level attributes | Base projection to join with set, legality, printing, price, or language-specific views while preserving card-level uniqueness | Compose further aggregations or metrics per card (e.g., counts of printings, available purchase links) by joining to exploded/aggregated siblings appropriately

params.metric: No aggregated measures are defined in this projection (grain = cards.id). All columns are passthrough attributes from cards. If you need counts or aggregates, compute them after joining to one-to-many sources and aggregating back to this card.id key. Example derived metric patterns that can be composed on top of this view: | printings_count = COUNT(distinct card_printings.printing_id) GROUP BY cards.id | available_purchase_sources = COUNT(distinct purchase_table.source) GROUP BY cards.id | min_price = MIN(prices.price) GROUP BY cards.id
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to set or set-level views on setCode — join to sets on cards.setCode = sets.code is safe because cards rows are one-per-card-printing (id) and sets is one-row-per-set; this will not duplicate card-level attributes. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to cards_color_identity_exploded on cards.id = cards_color_identity_exploded.id is NOT safe for naive SELECT * because cards_color_identity_exploded is one-to-many (one card -> multiple exploded color_identity rows). To preserve card-level measures, aggregate the exploded view back to cards.id (e.g., string_agg or array_agg) before joining, or join and then re-aggregate. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to card_legalities_current on cards.id = card_legalities_current.id is safe if card_legalities_current is a one-row-per-card (it is documented as AGG — check it returns one row per card). If card_legalities_current contains multiple rows per card for different formats, you must aggregate or filter to a single format before joining. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: do NOT join directly to card_rulings_latest or card_foreign_latest_per_language without ensuring they are one-row-per-card; these views are RANK-based and may be one-to-many (per language or multiple rulings). Either join on a composite key that guarantees one row (e.g., id + language + rank = 1), or aggregate their rows to cards.id first (e.g., latest_ruling_text = MIN/ARRAY_AGG filtered to latest). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: joining to cards_edhrec_rank_running (WIN) may be unsafe if it contains multiple time-series rows per card. Aggregate or filter to the desired partition (latest) before joining to avoid multiplying rows/metrics. | General rule: This projection is one-row-per-cards.id. Any join to a dimension that is also one-row-per-key (set metadata, canonical card metadata keyed by id or uuid) will not duplicate rows. Any join to tables/views that are one-to-many (printings list, exploded color identity, rulings, foreign translations, price history) WILL multiply rows unless those tables are pre-aggregated or the join includes a deterministic single-row filter (e.g., latest per language). When composing metrics, always GROUP BY cards.id after joining one-to-many sources or perform subquery aggregation keyed by cards.id before joining.

views.description: Normalized projection of the cards table preserving key identifiers and exposing commonly used descriptive and measure columns. Useful as a base relation for joins, filtering cohorts, and analytics that need card-level attributes without modifying original column names. | Use for: list cards with specific attributes (rarity, setCode, colors); base card metadata for joining to legalities/sets/foreign_data; filter and aggregate card measures like convertedManaCost or edhrecRank

views.name: cards_with_set
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.id,
  c.uuid,
  c.name,
  c.setCode,
  c.number,
  c.rarity,
  c.type,
  c.colors,
  c.convertedManaCost,
  c.edhrecRank,
  s.id AS id_1,
  s.code,
  s.name AS name_1,
  s.block,
  s.type AS type_1,
  s.releaseDate,
  s.baseSetSize,
  s.totalSetSize
FROM cards c
LEFT JOIN sets s
  ON c.setCode = s.code

params.description: Provides one row per card (cards.id) enriched with its set record where available — useful for card-level reporting with set attributes.
params.when_to_use: Fetch card details together with the set the card belongs to (set metadata like name, release date, sizes). | Filter or group cards by set attributes (set code, set name, block, releaseDate) while keeping card-level grain. | Join card-level measures (counts, prices, edhrecRank) to set metadata for display or aggregation. | As a building block for composing further card-level queries that need set context without rejoining sets.
params.output_schema: id: primary key of the view — cards.id from table cards (one row per card). | uuid: cards.uuid — card unique identifier (likely a GUID) from cards.uuid. | name: cards.name — card name from cards.name. | setCode: cards.setCode — set code on the card (FK-ish) from cards.setCode used to join to sets.code. | number: cards.number — the collector number on the card from cards.number. | rarity: cards.rarity — rarity text from cards.rarity. | type: cards.type — card type line from cards.type. | colors: cards.colors — card colors representation from cards.colors. | convertedManaCost: cards.convertedManaCost — numeric converted mana cost from cards.convertedManaCost. | edhrecRank: cards.edhrecRank — numeric EDHREC popularity rank from cards.edhrecRank. | id_1: sets.id — the set's internal id (renamed id_1 in the SELECT) from sets.id. | code: sets.code — set code from sets.code (same values as cards.setCode when joined). | name_1: sets.name — set name (renamed name_1) from sets.name. | block: sets.block — set block/series from sets.block. | type_1: sets.type — set type (renamed type_1) from sets.type. | releaseDate: sets.releaseDate — set release/releaseDate from sets.releaseDate. | baseSetSize: sets.baseSetSize — base set size from sets.baseSetSize. | totalSetSize: sets.totalSetSize — total set size from sets.totalSetSize.
params.grounded_columns: cards.id | cards.uuid | cards.name | cards.setCode | cards.number | cards.rarity | cards.type | cards.colors | cards.convertedManaCost | cards.edhrecRank | sets.id | sets.code | sets.name | sets.block | sets.type | sets.releaseDate | sets.baseSetSize | sets.totalSetSize
params.metric: This view is a projection/lookup and defines no aggregate measures. | derived columns are direct passthroughs; e.g., convertedManaCost = cards.convertedManaCost (no aggregation). | No aggregated metric is present in this view; any aggregations (counts, sums, averages) must be computed by consumers at their chosen grain.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: |  - Safe to join this view to one-row-per-set dimension (sets at set code/id) on setCode = code or id = id_1: joining to a set dimension does NOT duplicate card rows because this view already contains the set attributes via a LEFT JOIN (one set row per card at most). |  - Safe to join to strictly one-to-one or many-to-one dimensions keyed at card id (for example a cards_base_projection or any table/view where card.id is the primary key) on id = id: such joins will not multiply rows because this view is one-row-per-cards.id. |  - Do NOT blind-join this view to one-to-many tables keyed by card id (examples: card_rulings_latest if it is one-to-many per card, cards_color_identity_exploded which is an exploded color-per-card reshape, or any legalities/history tables that contain multiple rows per card) without first aggregating or deduplicating the many-side. Reason: those joins would multiply this view's card-level rows and thereby duplicate any downstream aggregates derived from the card grain. |  - If you need to attach one-to-many data (rulings, translations, multiple foreign-language rows, exploded colors), either: |      * join to an already-aggregated/rolled-up view (one row per card) that summarizes that many-side, or |      * pre-aggregate after joining (e.g., GROUP BY cards_with_set.id and apply aggregate functions), or |      * join using lateral/array_agg approaches that preserve one output row per card. |  - Examples of safe compositions: |      * cards_with_set JOIN cards_base_projection USING (id) — safe if cards_base_projection is one-row-per-card. |      * cards_with_set aggregated by setCode to compute cards count per set: SELECT setCode, COUNT(*) FROM cards_with_set GROUP BY setCode — correct because the view is at card grain. |  - Examples of unsafe compositions without re-aggregation: |      * cards_with_set JOIN cards_color_identity_exploded ON cards_with_set.id = cards_color_identity_exploded.id — unsafe (many colors per card) unless you aggregate colors first. |      * cards_with_set JOIN card_rulings_latest ON id = card_rulings_latest.card_id — unsafe if multiple rulings rows exist per card; aggregate rulings first.

views.description: Denormalized relation joining cards to their set metadata. One row per card (card printing) augmented with set attributes for contextual queries about releaseDate, set name, block, and size. Use when you need card attributes together with set-level metadata. | Use for: cards released in sets within a date range; compare card attributes with set properties (set size, block); list cards along with their set names and release dates

views.name: card_legalities_current
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  uuid,
  COUNT(*) AS format_count,
  GROUP_CONCAT(format, ',') AS formats_list
FROM legalities
GROUP BY uuid

params.description: For each card (uuid) returns how many distinct legality rows exist and a comma-concatenated list of their format values (current legalities per card).
params.when_to_use: Get the count of legality records per card (e.g., how many formats a card has legality entries for). | Show or filter cards by which formats they have legalities in using the comma-list. | As a building block when composing card-level queries that need card-wise legality counts or a compact formats list (must be joined carefully to avoid duplication). | Aggregate legalities up to the card grain before joining to other card-level data (to avoid double-counting).
params.output_schema: uuid: the card unique identifier (source: legalities.uuid) | format_count: integer count of legality rows for that uuid (derived from COUNT(*) over legalities grouped by legalities.uuid) | formats_list: a comma-separated string of the format values for that uuid (derived from GROUP_CONCAT(legalities.format, ','))
params.metric: format_count = COUNT(*) -- count of rows in legalities per legalities.uuid | formats_list = GROUP_CONCAT(format, ',') -- concatenation of legalities.format values per legalities.uuid
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to cards_base_projection (or any one-row-per-uuid card dimension/view) on card_legalities_current.uuid = cards_base_projection.uuid — safe because card_legalities_current is aggregated to one row per uuid, so joining to another one-row-per-uuid source will not duplicate measures. | Safe to join to cards_with_set, card_foreign_latest_per_language, card_rulings_latest, set_translations_per_language, cards_color_identity_exploded, cards_edhrec_rank_running only if those sibling views are also one-row-per-uuid; verify their grains before joining. If they are one-row-per-uuid, join on uuid is safe and will not duplicate format_count. | Do NOT join card_legalities_current directly to any one-to-many child table/view (for example, a raw legalities table, or any view that can have multiple rows per uuid) without re-aggregating the downstream side first, because that would multiply format_count and distort counts. | If you need to combine this view with a one-to-many detail (e.g., card rulings or multiple sets per card), either: (a) aggregate the detail to one row per uuid before joining, or (b) join first and then re-aggregate measures (e.g., SUM(format_count) over uuid after grouping) to avoid double-counting. | When composing additional metrics that count legalities across joined dimensions, prefer to re-compute counts from legalities directly or join this view and treat format_count as already-aggregated (do not sum it again across duplicated uuid rows).

views.description: Aggregated snapshot of legalities per card (uuid) producing a concatenated list of formats and a count of formats. Grain: one row per card (uuid). Useful for filtering cards by how many formats they're legal in or for quickly seeing which formats apply to a card. | Use for: find cards legal in a given number of formats; join legalities summary to cards to filter by format membership; reporting on format coverage across cards

views.name: card_foreign_latest_per_language
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  uuid,
  language,
  name,
  text,
  flavorText
FROM (
  SELECT
    fd.*, 
    RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY uuid, language ORDER BY id DESC) AS row_rank
  FROM foreign_data fd
) WHERE row_rank = 1

params.description: Latest foreign-language row per card UUID and language from the foreign_data table (one row per uuid + language, choosing the record with highest id).
params.when_to_use: Retrieve the most recent foreign-language name/text/flavorText for a given card UUID in a specific language. | Compose with card-level base data when you need the latest localized strings alongside canonical card identifiers (uuid or id). | Filter or aggregate counts of cards by language using the latest available foreign-language entry per card. | Join into higher-level reports that display a single localized label/description per card-language pair without duplications from historical foreign_data rows.
params.output_schema: id: primary key of the chosen foreign_data row (derived from foreign_data.id) | uuid: card UUID this foreign row is associated with (derived from foreign_data.uuid) | language: language code/identifier for this foreign entry (derived from foreign_data.language) | name: localized card name in this language (derived from foreign_data.name) | text: localized oracle/rules text in this language (derived from foreign_data.text) | flavorText: localized flavor text in this language (derived from foreign_data.flavorText)
params.grounded_columns: foreign_data.id | foreign_data.uuid | foreign_data.language | foreign_data.name | foreign_data.text | foreign_data.flavorText
params.metric: row_rank = RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY foreign_data.uuid, foreign_data.language ORDER BY foreign_data.id DESC) | Note: the view filters WHERE row_rank = 1 to produce the latest row per (uuid, language). There are no aggregated numeric metrics produced by this view.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to cards_base_projection (or any one-row-per-uuid base card view) on card_foreign_latest_per_language.uuid = cards_base_projection.uuid — safe because card_base is one-row-per-uuid and this view is one-row-per-(uuid,language); joining will not duplicate rows per (uuid,language). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to set_translations_per_language on (language, set_id) only when set_translations_per_language is one-row-per-(set_id,language); safe if that view guarantees one row per set+language. Confirm its grain before joining. | do NOT directly join to one-to-many sibling views without re-aggregation: examples of unsafe joins include joining to card_rulings_latest (if that view contains multiple rulings per uuid) or card_legalities_current (if it contains multiple rows per uuid) without ensuring those sibling views are at a compatible grain. Such joins would multiply rows per (uuid,language) and thereby duplicate this view's measures. | If you need to combine with multi-row resources (rulings, legalities, color_identity_exploded, edhrec running ranks across dates), either: (a) aggregate those resources up to uuid-level (or uuid+language if you need language-specific metrics) before joining, or (b) join first and then re-aggregate the combined result to the intended grain to avoid measure duplication. | When joining to cards_with_set (which likely is one-row-per-card-with-set), join on uuid (card_foreign_latest_per_language.uuid = cards_with_set.uuid) — safe if cards_with_set is one-row-per-uuid; verify that cards_with_set does not explode set membership into multiple rows per uuid. | General rule: this view exposes descriptive string fields (name, text, flavorText) and not numeric aggregates. Any join that duplicates rows will duplicate those descriptive rows; to preserve correctness, ensure the joined-to side is at most one row per uuid (or per uuid+language) or aggregate the other side first.

views.description: Latest foreign-language row per card UUID and language from the foreign_data table (one row per uuid + language, choosing the record with highest id).

views.name: card_rulings_latest
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  uuid,
  date,
  text
FROM (
  SELECT
    r.*, 
    RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY uuid ORDER BY date DESC, id DESC) AS ruling_rank
  FROM rulings r
) WHERE ruling_rank = 1

params.description: Latest ruling per card UUID (most recent by date, tiebreak by id).
params.when_to_use: Get the most recent ruling text and date for a specific card (by uuid or id). | Join latest ruling information onto card-level queries where exactly one ruling per card is required. | Compose into aggregates that count or list cards with/without a latest ruling, or compute metrics that rely on a single canonical ruling row per card.
params.output_schema: id: the primary key id of the selected ruling row from the base table `rulings.id` (source: rulings.id) | uuid: the card UUID that this ruling pertains to from `rulings.uuid` (source: rulings.uuid) | date: the ruling's date from `rulings.date` (source: rulings.date) | text: the ruling text/content from `rulings.text` (source: rulings.text)
params.metric: ruling_rank = RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY rulings.uuid ORDER BY rulings.date DESC, rulings.id DESC) | Note: the view projects rows where ruling_rank = 1, effectively selecting the latest ruling per uuid by date with id as a deterministic tiebreaker.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to cards_base_projection or cards_with_set on uuid (e.g. ON card_rulings_latest.uuid = cards_base_projection.uuid) — safe because card_rulings_latest is one-row-per-uuid so its columns will not be duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to cards_color_identity_exploded on uuid only if you first aggregate or deduplicate the exploded rows by uuid; joining directly will multiply this view's rows because cards_color_identity_exploded is one-to-many (one card -> many exploded rows). | do NOT join directly to card_foreign_latest_per_language, set_translations_per_language, or any other sibling view that is one-to-many per uuid without aggregation (e.g. grouping or choosing a single row per uuid) because those joins will duplicate the latest-ruling row and thus multiply any measures derived from this view. | When composing metrics that count rulings or compute sums/rates, treat card_rulings_latest as a dimension-level (one-row-per-card) view. If you need to join to one-to-many detail tables (for example, language variants or multiple legalities), first aggregate those tables to one row per uuid (e.g. ARRAY_AGG, MAX, COUNT) before joining to avoid duplicating the latest-ruling row. | If you need to join on rulings.id to another table keyed to a specific ruling row, joining on id is safe because id is unique per ruling row in the base table. | If combining with card_legalities_current (an aggregate) ensure that card_legalities_current is also one-row-per-uuid (or aggregated to uuid) so the join remains cardinality-safe.

views.description: Latest ruling per card (uuid) based on date and id as tiebreaker. One row per card exposing the most recent ruling text and date. Useful when you only need the current/latest ruling attached to a card. | Use for: attach latest ruling to cards; list cards with their most recent ruling; filter cards that have rulings after/before a date

views.name: set_translations_per_language
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  setCode,
  language,
  translation
FROM set_translations

params.description: Translations of a card set per language (one row per set-translation).
params.when_to_use: Find the translation text for a specific set code and language | List all languages available for a given set (setCode) | Join set translations to card or set-level data when you need the localized set name/translation | Compose with aggregations over translations (e.g., count languages per set) | Filter cards by set and present the set name in the desired language
params.output_schema: id: surrogate/primary id for the translation row — derived from set_translations.id | setCode: set identifier/code that this translation belongs to — derived from set_translations.setCode | language: language code/identifier for this translation (e.g., 'en', 'fr') — derived from set_translations.language | translation: localized translation text for the set — derived from set_translations.translation
params.metric: id = identity(set_translations.id) | setCode = identity(set_translations.setCode) | language = identity(set_translations.language) | translation = identity(set_translations.translation) | languages_per_set = COUNT(language) -- not provided by this view directly; to compute, aggregate this view by setCode: SELECT setCode, COUNT(*) AS languages_per_set FROM set_translations_per_language GROUP BY setCode
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a one-row-per-set view or table on setCode — safe because set_translations_per_language is one-row-per-(id) translation but only one translation row per (setCode, language). Examples: join to a sets_master_view on setCode when that view is one-row-per-set, but be aware that joining without restricting language will multiply the set row per available language. If you intend not to multiply, restrict language first or aggregate translations into one value. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to cards_base_projection (or cards_with_set) on setCode — careful: cards tables are typically one-row-per-card. Joining cards (one-to-many: many cards -> one set) to set_translations_per_language (one-to-many: many translations per set) will produce a multiplicative result equal to (#cards in set) * (#translations for set) unless you pre-filter translations to a single language or aggregate translations (e.g., pick MAX(translation) FILTER (WHERE language='en')). To avoid duplication of card-level measures, either: | - restrict set_translations_per_language to a single language in the join condition (e.g., ... AND set_translations_per_language.language = 'en'), or | - aggregate translations to one row per setCode (e.g., JSON_AGG or STRING_AGG by language) before joining, or | - aggregate card measures after the join and divide/adjust as appropriate (not recommended). | do NOT join without re-aggregation to one-to-many views such as card_rulings_latest, card_foreign_latest_per_language, cards_color_identity_exploded, card_legalities_current, cards_edhrec_rank_running when those are many-rows-per-card, because combining two one-to-many sides via setCode or card id will multiply rows and duplicate measures. Instead, join each one-to-many to the card/set primary side or pre-aggregate them to one row per join key. | safe composition patterns: | - To annotate cards with a single-language set name: join cards_with_set c -> set_translations_per_language t ON c.setCode = t.setCode AND t.language = '<lang>' (safe: one translation per set for that language). | - To compute languages-per-set: aggregate this view by setCode: SELECT setCode, COUNT(*) AS language_count FROM set_translations_per_language GROUP BY setCode (safe: produces one row per setCode). | - To produce a per-card result with localized set name without duplication: first select translations filtered to the desired language (or aggregated to one value per setCode), then join to cards_base_projection or cards_with_set. | explicit caution: because this view exposes translations at the translation-row grain (one row per id/ language), joining it directly to another one-to-many dataset on setCode will multiply that dataset's measures by the number of translations for that set. Always ensure either the join target is one-row-per-set (so no duplication), or translations are reduced to one row per setCode (via filter or aggregation) before joining.

views.description: Simple selection of set_translations preserving setCode, language and translation. Use to join localized set names to sets or cards. This CTE is a direct pass-through and useful as a stable translation lookup. | Use for: join translated set names to sets or cards; filter sets by available translation languages
validated_on: How many Brazilian Portuguese translated sets are inside the Commander block?

views.name: cards_color_identity_exploded
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.id,
  c.uuid,
  TRIM(
    CASE WHEN instr(ci.value, ',') = 0 THEN ci.value
         ELSE substr(ci.value, 1, instr(ci.value, ',')-1)
    END
  ) AS colorIdentity_token
FROM (
  SELECT id, uuid,
    CASE WHEN colorIdentity IS NULL OR TRIM(colorIdentity) = '' THEN NULL
         ELSE colorIdentity END AS colorIdentity
  FROM cards
) AS c
JOIN (
  SELECT id AS _id, 
         -- for SQLite without a splitter, expose the full string as single value;
         -- consumers can replace this subselect with a proper splitter that yields rows per token
         colorIdentity AS value
  FROM (
    SELECT id, colorIdentity FROM cards
  )
) AS ci ON ci._id = c.id

params.when_to_use: Ask for each card's individual colorIdentity token (first token when comma-separated) for filtering or grouping by single token. | Compose into queries that need to treat colorIdentity tokens as rows (e.g., count cards per color token) when the consumer will ensure full splitting if required. | Join to card-level dimensions or lookups on card id without changing card-level cardinality.

If colorIdentity contains a comma, this is the substring up to the first comma (trimmed). If colorIdentity is NULL or empty it will not appear because upstream NULLs are filtered out by c.colorIdentity being NULL=>NULL (see SQL). Sourced from the ci.value which is populated from cards.colorIdentity.
params.metric: colorIdentity_token = TRIM(CASE WHEN instr(ci.value, ',') = 0 THEN ci.value ELSE substr(ci.value, 1, instr(ci.value, ',')-1) END) | note: there are no aggregate metrics in this view; all outputs are direct projections or string expressions of base columns.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to card-level dimensions or views (one row per cards.id) on cards.id (this view's id) — examples: join to cards_base_projection on id, join to cards_with_set on id, join to card_foreign_latest_per_language on id (if that view is one-row-per-card), because this view is one-row-per (id, colorIdentity_token) and joining to another one-row-per-card view on id will not multiply card-level measures. | Do NOT blindly join to one-to-many child tables or views (e.g., card_rulings_latest if it is multi-row per card, any rulings or multiple-set printings or translations that are many-per-card) without re-aggregation, because those joins will multiply rows and duplicate measures derived from this view. If you must join to a one-to-many relation, either: |   - aggregate the child side to one row per cards.id before joining (e.g., count or max), or |   - join first to a distinct list of cards.id (or this view) and then lateral/exists-check the many-side to avoid duplication. | Special note about splitting: this view's ci subquery currently exposes the full colorIdentity string as a single value per card; it does not truly explode multi-token values into multiple rows. If you need full multi-token explosion (one output row per token when colorIdentity contains multiple comma-separated tokens), replace/augment the ci subquery with a proper splitter that returns one row per token. Until then, this view yields at most one token per card (the first token).

views.description: Unpivots the cards.colorIdentity (comma/concatenated string) into one row per card per color identity token. Produces rows for each color symbol found in colorIdentity to support color-level aggregation and filtering. Useful when colorIdentity contains multiple tokens separated by commas or no separator. | Use for: count cards by individual color identity; filter cards that include a specific color symbol

views.name: cards_edhrec_rank_running
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  uuid,
  name,
  edhrecRank,
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY edhrecRank ASC, id ASC) AS edhrec_rank_overall
FROM cards
WHERE edhrecRank IS NOT NULL

params.description: Provides one-row-per-card (by id) EDHREC popularity rank for cards that have an edhrecRank, plus a dense overall ordering of those ranks.
params.when_to_use: Find a card's EDHREC rank or compare EDHREC ranks across cards | Build leaderboards or sorted lists of cards by EDHREC popularity (ascending rank = more popular) | Compose into queries that need a stable per-card EDHREC rank value or a global rank ordering of cards with EDHREC data | Join card metadata to EDHREC rank when producing reports that must not duplicate rank measures
params.output_schema: id: unique surrogate integer id for the card (source: cards.id) | uuid: card UUID string (source: cards.uuid) | name: card name string (source: cards.name) | edhrecRank: numeric EDHREC rank for the card (source: cards.edhrecRank) | edhrec_rank_overall: integer rank computed as RANK() OVER (ORDER BY edhrecRank ASC, id ASC) — a 1-based ordering across all cards with non-null edhrecRank (derived expression)
params.metric: edhrecRank = cards.edhrecRank (pass-through metric / base column) | edhrec_rank_overall = RANK() OVER (ORDER BY cards.edhrecRank ASC, cards.id ASC) (window ranking expression computed across the filtered set WHERE cards.edhrecRank IS NOT NULL)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to cards_base_projection (NORM) on id — safe because both are one-row-per-card keyed by cards.id, so edhrecRank and edhrec_rank_overall remain one value per resulting row and are not duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to cards_with_set (JOIN) on id — safe if cards_with_set is one-row-per-card; confirm that view is one-row-per-id before joining. If it is one-row-per-id, joining preserves one-row-per-card semantics and does not duplicate measures. | Do NOT directly join to one-to-many views/tables such as card_rulings_latest (RANK) or card_foreign_latest_per_language (RANK) or cards_color_identity_exploded (RESHAPE) without aggregation, because those are or may be one-to-many relative to card id and will duplicate edhrecRank and edhrec_rank_overall across multiple rows for the same card. If you need EDHREC measures alongside such one-to-many detail, either: | - aggregate the one-to-many side back to one row per cards.id before joining (e.g., ARRAY_AGG, MAX, COUNT, or other aggregation), or | - join this view first and then re-aggregate after the join while applying an appropriate aggregation function to avoid multiplying rank values. | When composing global metrics (e.g., counts, averages) that include edhrecRank, prefer to compute aggregates from this view grouped by id (one row per card) to avoid bias introduced by joining to expanding relationships. | Because edhrec_rank_overall is computed with a window that only considers rows WHERE cards.edhrecRank IS NOT NULL, do not expect edhrec_rank_overall to be dense across all cards in the cards table; it's dense only among cards present in this view. If you need a ranking that includes cards with NULL edhrecRank, compute a different rank on the appropriate base table or add a COALESCE-ed surrogate value before ranking.

views.description: Compute a running rank of cards ordered by edhrecRank (lower is more popular) with ties broken by id. Useful for downstream Top-K logic where consumers will filter by rank <= K. | Use for: top-N most popular cards by edhrecRank; rank-based filters for popularity

views.name: cards_with_english_text_fallback
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  cbp.id AS id,
  cbp.uuid AS uuid,
  cbp.name AS name,
  cbp.setCode AS setCode,
  -- Prefer cards text when non-null and not empty, otherwise use English foreign text
  CASE
    WHEN cbp.text IS NOT NULL AND trim(cbp.text) <> '' THEN cbp.text
    WHEN fed.text IS NOT NULL AND trim(fed.text) <> '' THEN fed.text
    ELSE NULL
  END AS text_final,
  cbp.originalText AS originalText,
  CASE
    WHEN cbp.text IS NOT NULL AND trim(cbp.text) <> '' THEN 'cards'
    WHEN fed.text IS NOT NULL AND trim(fed.text) <> '' THEN 'foreign_data_en'
    ELSE 'none'
  END AS text_source
FROM cards_base_projection cbp
LEFT JOIN foreign_english_texts_by_card_uuid fed
  ON cbp.uuid = fed.uuid
views.description: Denormalized view that for each cards.id provides the preferred English oracle/rules text: preferentially cards.text if non-null/non-empty, otherwise English foreign_data.text. Also exposes which source supplied the text via a 'text_source' column.

params.description: Provides one-row-per-card (uuid) core card attributes useful for selecting, filtering, and joining basic card metadata.

params.output_schema: uuid: Unique card identifier; derived from cards.uuid | id: Human-readable or set-specific card id; derived from cards.id | name: Card name; derived from cards.name | setCode: Code of the set this card belongs to; derived from cards.setCode | borderColor: Border color attribute for the card; derived from cards.borderColor | colors: Card colors (likely array/text); derived from cards.colors | colorIdentity: Card color identity (likely array/text); derived from cards.colorIdentity | rarity: Card rarity (e.g., common/uncommon/rare/mythic); derived from cards.rarity | type: Card type line; derived from cards.type | releasedate: Original release date of the card; derived from cards.originalReleaseDate | hasFoil: Boolean/flag indicating if a foil printing exists; derived from cards.hasFoil | hasNonFoil: Boolean/flag indicating if a non-foil printing exists; derived from cards.hasNonFoil

params.metric: uuid = identity(cards.uuid) | id = identity(cards.id) | name = identity(cards.name) | setCode = identity(cards.setCode) | borderColor = identity(cards.borderColor) | colors = identity(cards.colors) | colorIdentity = identity(cards.colorIdentity) | rarity = identity(cards.rarity) | type = identity(cards.type) | releasedate = identity(cards.originalReleaseDate) | hasFoil = identity(cards.hasFoil) | hasNonFoil = identity(cards.hasNonFoil)

  CASE

params.output_schema: uuid: unique card identifier (derived from cards_base_projection.uuid) | id: card id field (derived from cards_base_projection.id) | borderColor: the card's borderColor value (derived from cards_base_projection.borderColor) | is_bordercolor_match: presence marker for borderColor; 1 when borderColor IS NOT NULL, 0 when borderColor IS NULL (derived from CASE WHEN cards_base_projection.borderColor IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END)
params.metric: is_bordercolor_match = CASE WHEN cards_base_projection.borderColor IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension-like, one-row-per-card views/tables on uuid — examples: cards_with_set (JOIN) on cards_with_set.uuid = cards_bordercolor_cohort.uuid — safe because cards_with_set is expected to be one-row-per-uuid so this view's one-row-per-uuid cardinality is preserved and its measures are not duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to cards_with_set_info (JOIN) on id or uuid when that view/table is one-row-per-card — safe for the same reason. | Do NOT directly join to one-to-many child tables/views without re-aggregation first: examples include card_rulings_latest (RANK) if it can produce multiple rows per uuid, card_foreign_latest_per_language (RANK) which is language-ranked and may produce multiple rows per uuid across languages, cards_foreign_texts_by_uuid (JOIN) which can be multi-row per uuid, cards_color_identity_exploded (RESHAPE) which explodes into multiple rows per card, and legalities_by_card (SEL) if it lists multiple legalities per card. Joining these directly will multiply rows and thus duplicate the is_bordercolor_match measure. | If you need to combine with a one-to-many source, first aggregate that source up to uuid (for example, take MAX or ARRAY_AGG as appropriate) so the join key is one-row-per-uuid and the composed query remains cardinality-safe. | Joins on id are allowed only when the other side is one-row-per-id; prefer joining on uuid for stability unless you know id is unique in the target source.

views.name: sets_basic

params.description: Provides one-row-per-set basic attributes (code, name, release date, type) from the sets table.
params.when_to_use: Return basic metadata for a single set or list of sets (code, human name, release date, set type). | Join as a dimension when assembling card-level records to bring in set attributes without changing cardinality (one set per set.code). | Filter or group results by set attributes (e.g., count cards per set.type or per releaseDate) when the aggregation is applied after joining. | Serve as the foundational projection when composing translations or other set-level enrichments.
params.output_schema: code: Set identifier/code — derived from sets.code | name: The human-readable set name — derived from sets.name | releaseDate: The set's official release date — derived from sets.releaseDate | type: The set's classification/type (e.g., core, expansion) — derived from sets.type

params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to cards_base_projection or cards_with_set on cards.set_code = sets.code — safe because sets is one-row-per code (the view's grain is ['code']) so joining will not duplicate set-level attributes; any measures originating from sets are not duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to set_translations_per_language on set_translations_per_language.set_code = sets.code — safe if you intend to bring translation rows; note this will produce multiple rows per set if translation table is many-to-one per language, so only do this when you expect one translation row per set-language or when the downstream logic can handle multiple rows. | do NOT blindly join to one-to-many tables (for example: cards_foreign_latest_per_language, card_rulings_latest, cards_foreign_texts_by_uuid, cards_color_identity_exploded, etc.) without controlling cardinality — these are one-to-many relative to sets (they are one-to-many via cards or translations) and will multiply rows derived from sets. If you need aggregated set-level metrics from those tables, first aggregate them to one row per sets.code (e.g., COUNT(...), MAX(...), ARRAY_AGG(...) grouped by set_code) and then join to this view to preserve one-row-per-set semantics. | When composing into dashboards or further views that count or sum cards by set, prefer joining this view to an aggregated cards-level source (e.g., cards_base_projection aggregated by set_code) or join cards and then GROUP BY sets.code to avoid accidental duplication of set-level measures. | Example safe pattern: SELECT s.code, s.name, COUNT(c.uuid) AS card_count FROM sets_basic s JOIN cards_base_projection c ON c.set_code = s.code GROUP BY s.code, s.name — this counts cards per set correctly because card counting is performed after join and grouped back to set keys. | Example unsafe pattern: joining sets_basic to a card_rulings_latest view on set code without aggregation may produce N x M rows when multiple rulings or languages exist per set; to be safe, aggregate rulings to one row per set (e.g., latest_ruling_text_per_set) before joining.

views.name: cards_story_spotlight_flag

SELECT

FROM cards

params.description: Provides a one-row-per-card UUID flag indicating whether that card is marked as a Story Spotlight (normalized to 0/1).
params.when_to_use: Ask whether a specific card (by uuid) is a Story Spotlight | Filter or group cards by Story Spotlight status when building card-level queries | Compose into larger card-level datasets where a stable binary flag per card is needed
params.output_schema: uuid: the card's canonical unique identifier (derived from cards.uuid) | isStorySpotlight: binary indicator (0 or 1) showing whether the source cards.isStorySpotlight value denotes a Story Spotlight; mapped from cards.isStorySpotlight via a truthy test
params.metric: isStorySpotlight = CASE WHEN cards.isStorySpotlight IN (1, '1', 't', 'true', 'TRUE', 'True') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to card-level one-row-per-uuid dimensions or views on uuid — safe because cards_story_spotlight_flag is one-row-per-uuid and thus its binary measure will not be duplicated. Example safe joins: cards_base_projection on uuid; cards_with_set_info on uuid (if those views are one-row-per-uuid). | Do NOT join directly to one-to-many child tables/views (e.g., card_rulings_latest, card_foreign_latest_per_language, cards_foreign_texts_by_uuid, cards_color_identity_exploded) without first aggregating those children back to one row per uuid. Joining a one-to-many will multiply rows and implicitly duplicate the isStorySpotlight flag unless you re-aggregate (e.g., use MAX(isStorySpotlight) after the join or aggregate the child rows to one row per uuid before joining). | If composing aggregates across related tables, treat isStorySpotlight as a deterministic per-uuid attribute. For example, to compute counts by spotlight status from a one-to-many source, first aggregate the one-to-many to one row per uuid (e.g., count/rank/etc.), then join to cards_story_spotlight_flag on uuid, or join first and then aggregate using MAX(isStorySpotlight) to avoid duplication. | Joins to sibling one-row-per-uuid views (cards_base_projection, cards_with_set, cards_with_set_info, card_legalities_current if guaranteed one row per card) are safe. Validate the sibling view's grain before joining: if a sibling view uses aggregation or ranking but can produce multiple rows per uuid (e.g., card_foreign_latest_per_language produces multiple rows per language), treat it as a many-side and aggregate first.

params.metric: cards.isStorySpotlight = cards_story_spotlight_flag.isStorySpotlight  -- passthrough boolean flag (no aggregation) | There are no aggregated measures in this view; all outputs are direct column projections.

If you need attributes from a one-to-many source, first aggregate that source to one row per uuid (e.g., latest, array_agg, count, max) and then join. | Do NOT join this view directly to card-level aggregate views that themselves aggregate over foreign_data.id unless the aggregator's grain matches foreign_data.id, because mismatched grains can cause duplication or incorrect aggregation. | Recommended composition pattern: (1) if adding one-to-one card attributes, join on uuid directly; (2) if adding many-side attributes, pre-aggregate to one row per uuid (or per foreign_data.id if appropriate) before joining to preserve cardinality and avoid duplicating the cards.isStorySpotlight flag.

views.name: cards_row_level

params.description: Provides one-row-per-card identifiers and basic textual attributes (id, uuid, name, originalType, subtypes) from the cards_base_projection table.
params.when_to_use: Lookup a card's canonical identifiers and primary text fields by id or uuid. | As the single-row seed when composing wider card-level queries (joins or aggregates) that must start from one row per card. | Filtering or selecting cards by name, originalType, or subtypes before joining to other card-level or many-to-one datasets.
params.output_schema: id: integer — the primary card id, sourced from cards_base_projection.id | uuid: text — card UUID, sourced from cards_base_projection.uuid | name: text|null — trimmed card name; empty strings are normalized to NULL using NULLIF(TRIM(cbp.name),'') — sourced from cards_base_projection.name | originalType: text|null — trimmed originalText (interpreted as card type text); empty strings normalized to NULL using NULLIF(TRIM(cbp.originalText),'') — sourced from cards_base_projection.originalText | subtypes: text|null — trimmed subtypes string (may contain subtype tokens); empty strings normalized to NULL using NULLIF(TRIM(cbp.subtypes),'') — sourced from cards_base_projection.subtypes

Doing so will multiply rows and duplicate this view's measures. | If you need attributes from one-to-many siblings (example: rulings, foreign texts, exploded color identities, per-language sets), either: (a) join to an aggregated view keyed by id/uuid that returns one row per card (e.g., an AGG or SEL sibling that reduces multiplicity), or (b) perform the join and then re-aggregate measures at the card id grain to avoid double-counting. | When joining by uuid instead of id, ensure the target view/table has unique uuid (or is aggregated) — otherwise treat it as a potential many-side and aggregate first. | This view contains no native numeric metrics (no aggregates). Any derived metrics (counts, sums) computed after joining must be computed with awareness of join multiplicity; prefer pre-aggregated siblings (e.g., card_legalities_current which is AGG) to preserve cardinality safety.

views.name: cards_type_subtype_cohort

  cbp.id,

  cbp.name,

    WHEN cbp.subtypes IS NOT NULL

params.description: Returns one row per card id with its uuid, name, original type text, the raw subtypes string, and a boolean flag indicating whether the subtype text contains 'angel'.
params.when_to_use: Fetch card identity and type/cohort-related attributes (id, uuid, name, original type, subtypes) for use in UI lists or further SQL composition. | Filter or group cards by presence of the 'angel' subtype (has_subtype_angel) without parsing subtype tokens client-side. | Join card-level metadata into wider card result sets where one-row-per-card is required. | Compose higher-level aggregations that need type/cohort attributes as dimensions (e.g., counts by originalType or has_subtype_angel).

Such joins will multiply rows and duplicate this view's columns/flags. | If you need to enrich with one-to-many data, first aggregate the child table to one row per cards_base_projection.id (for example: ARRAY_AGG, MAX, COUNT, or a filtered RANK to pick a single row) and then join to this view on id to remain cardinality-safe. | When joining by uuid instead of id, ensure the target view/table has at most one row per uuid; otherwise re-aggregate on uuid first. This view is one-row-per-id; relying on id is the canonical safe key. | Because has_subtype_angel is derived purely from cards_base_projection.subtypes (a base column), it will remain correct after any safe one-row-per-card join. If you join to a dataset that expands rows, re-compute or re-aggregate the flag after the join to avoid incorrect multiplicative counts.

views.name: cards_with_foreign_and_legal_meta
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.id AS id,
  c.uuid AS uuid,
  c.name AS name,
  c.originalType AS originalType,
  c.subtypes AS subtypes,
  COALESCE(fd.foreign_count, 0) AS foreign_count,
  COALESCE(lg.legalities_count, 0) AS legalities_count
FROM cards AS c
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    uuid,
    COUNT(*) AS foreign_count
  FROM foreign_data
  GROUP BY uuid
) AS fd ON fd.uuid = c.uuid
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    uuid,
    COUNT(*) AS legalities_count
  FROM legalities
  GROUP BY uuid
) AS lg ON lg.uuid = c.uuid

params.description: Per-card projection that returns basic card identity and text/meta fields plus counts of related foreign_data rows and legalities rows per card (grouped by card UUID).
params.when_to_use: Get a list of cards with their id/uuid/name/type/subtypes and how many foreign_data and legalities records exist for each card. | Compose dashboards or downstream SQL that needs per-card counts of foreign entries or legalities without re-aggregating foreign_data or legalities repeatedly. | Filter or join cards while preserving per-card aggregated counts (e.g., show cards with at least N foreign versions or K legalities). | Use as a one-row-per-card building block when joining to dimensions keyed by card id or uuid (so measures remain one-per-card).
params.output_schema: id: primary numeric id for the card from cards.id (cards.id) | uuid: canonical card UUID from cards.uuid (cards.uuid) | name: card name from cards.name (cards.name) | originalType: card's originalType string from cards.originalType (cards.originalType) | subtypes: card's subtypes value from cards.subtypes (cards.subtypes) | foreign_count: integer count of rows in foreign_data that share this card's uuid (derived from aggregate COUNT(*) grouped by foreign_data.uuid) | legalities_count: integer count of rows in legalities that share this card's uuid (derived from aggregate COUNT(*) grouped by legalities.uuid)
params.grounded_columns: cards.id | cards.uuid | cards.name | cards.originalType | cards.subtypes | foreign_data.uuid | legalities.uuid
params.metric: foreign_count = COALESCE((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM foreign_data fd WHERE fd.uuid = cards.uuid GROUP BY fd.uuid), 0) | legalities_count = COALESCE((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM legalities lg WHERE lg.uuid = cards.uuid GROUP BY lg.uuid), 0)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension/table keyed one-to-one with cards by cards.id or cards.uuid (for example: cards_with_set_info ON cards.id or cards.uuid) — safe because this view returns exactly one row per cards.id (grain = ['id']), so measures foreign_count and legalities_count are not duplicated. | Safe to join to normalized single-row-per-card projections such as cards_base_projection (if that view is one-row-per-card) or cards_with_set (if that view preserves one-row-per-card) on cards.id or cards.uuid because those joins do not increase cardinality. | Do NOT join this view directly to any one-to-many child tables or views (for example: foreign_data, legalities, cards_foreign_texts_by_uuid, cards_color_identity_exploded, card_rulings_latest when multiple rows per card exist, or any other multi-row-per-card view) without first aggregating the child to one row per card. Such joins will multiply foreign_count and legalities_count and therefore over-count measures. Instead, either: | - aggregate the child to one row per uuid/id (e.g., COUNT, MAX, ARRAY_AGG) and join on uuid or id, or | - join to a view that is already aggregated to one row per card (for example card_foreign_latest_per_language is a RANK view and may be multi-row; use a pre-aggregated version instead). | When joining across UUID vs id keys: this view uses cards.id as its grain and includes cards.uuid. If you join on cards.uuid to other tables keyed by uuid, cardinality remains one-to-one provided those other tables are one-row-per-uuid. If joining to tables keyed by cards.id, prefer joining on id for clarity and to match the declared grain. | If you need to combine the foreign_count or legalities_count with further aggregations (e.g., SUM of foreign_count across sets), aggregate these measures at the end of the query (e.g., SUM(foreign_count) GROUP BY ...) — do not pre-join to one-to-many tables that would cause duplication prior to aggregation.

views.description: Per-card projection that returns basic card identity and text/meta fields plus counts of related foreign_data rows and legalities rows per card (grouped by card UUID).

views.name: cards_base_row
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  uuid,
  name,
  setCode,
  duelDeck,
  types,
  colors,
  manaCost,
  rarity,
  isReprint
FROM cards

params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to views/tables that are one-row-per-card keyed by cards.id or cards.uuid without duplicating measures — safe examples: |  - Join to cards_base_projection on cards.id or cards.uuid — safe because both are one-row-per-card sources. |  - Join to cards_with_set or cards_with_set_info on setCode (or card id) when those views expose one-row-per-card — safe when their definition guarantees one row per card (verify sibling view contract before joining). |  - Join to legalities_by_card or card_legalities_current only when those views are aggregated to one-row-per-card (e.g., current legality summary); otherwise join will multiply rows. |  | Do NOT directly join without care to one-to-many child views/tables that expand a card into multiple rows, unless you re-aggregate after the join. views.name: cards_with_foreign_any

  c.id AS id,
  c.uuid AS uuid,
  c.name AS name,
  CASE WHEN COUNT(f.id) > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_foreign,
  COUNT(f.id) AS foreign_count
FROM cards c
LEFT JOIN foreign_data f ON f.uuid = c.uuid
GROUP BY c.id, c.uuid, c.name

params.description: For each card (id, uuid, name) indicates whether any foreign_data rows exist for that card and how many.
params.when_to_use: Get a per-card boolean flag and count of associated foreign_data rows (e.g., show if a card has any foreign printings and how many). | Filter cards by presence/absence of foreign entries (has_foreign = 1 or 0). | Join with other per-card data while preserving a single row per card and using foreign_count as a pre-aggregated metric. | Compose higher-level aggregations that need the count of foreign entries per card as an input metric (e.g., number of cards with at least one foreign printing per set).
params.output_schema: id: card primary key id from cards.id — the card table primary identifier used as the view grain | uuid: card uuid from cards.uuid — the card UUID used to join to foreign_data in the view | name: card name from cards.name — the card name present in cards | has_foreign: 1 if COUNT(f.id) > 0 else 0 — derived boolean indicator computed from COUNT(f.id) in the LEFT JOIN aggregation | foreign_count: integer COUNT(f.id) — the count of foreign_data rows matching the card's uuid as computed by the GROUP BY
params.metric: has_foreign = CASE WHEN COUNT(foreign_data.id) > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END | foreign_count = COUNT(foreign_data.id)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to per-card (one-row-per-card) views/tables on cards.id or cards.uuid — safe because cards_with_foreign_any is grouped at the card grain (id, uuid, name) and thus is one-row-per-card, so its measures will not be duplicated. Example: join to cards_base_projection ON id or uuid; join to cards_with_set_info ON id if that view is also one-row-per-card. | Safe to join to normalization/one-row-per-card siblings: cards_base_projection (NORM) on cards.id or cards.uuid — no duplication of foreign_count/has_foreign. | Safe to join to card-level aggregates (one-row-per-card): card_legalities_current (AGG) on id/uuid — no duplication because those siblings are also per-card aggregated. | Do NOT directly join (without re-aggregation) to any one-to-many child/detail tables or views that are multi-row per card, because that will multiply foreign_count and break the pre-aggregation. Examples of unsafe joins without re-aggregation: join to card_rulings_latest (RANK) if it yields multiple rows per card, cards_foreign_texts_by_uuid (JOIN) if that view is multi-row per uuid, cards_color_identity_exploded (RESHAPE) which expands colors to multiple rows per card, set_translations_per_language if it is multi-row per set and you join via set association, or any raw foreign_data table again. | If you must join to a multi-row-per-card view/table, first aggregate that side to one row per card (e.g., COUNT, MAX, STRING_AGG) and then join. Alternatively, join in a lateral/derived subquery that preserves aggregation per card to avoid duplicating foreign_count. | When composing higher-level metrics that sum foreign_count across groups (e.g., foreign_count per set), aggregate foreign_count after joining or prefer summarizing cards_with_foreign_any by the grouping key to avoid double-counting: SUM(foreign_count) after grouping by set is correct because foreign_count is already per-card.

views.name: card_with_foreign_and_legal_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.uuid AS uuid,
  COALESCE(fd.foreign_count, 0) AS foreign_count,
  COALESCE(lg.legalities_count, 0) AS legalities_count
FROM cards AS c
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    uuid,
    COUNT(*) AS foreign_count
  FROM foreign_data
  GROUP BY uuid
) AS fd ON fd.uuid = c.uuid
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    uuid,
    COUNT(*) AS legalities_count
  FROM legalities
  GROUP BY uuid
) AS lg ON lg.uuid = c.uuid

params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to any dimension or projection that is one-row-per-card keyed on cards.uuid (for example, cards_base_projection or cards_with_set_info keyed by uuid) — safe because this view is one-row-per-uuid so the measures (foreign_count, legalities_count) will not be duplicated. | Safe: join to cards_base_projection (NORM) ON uuid, because cards_base_projection is a normalized one-row-per-card projection; joining preserves one row per card. | Safe: join to cards_with_set_info (JOIN) ON uuid, if that view is one-row-per-card (it should be validated as one row per uuid); the pre-aggregated counts remain correct. | Do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables or views such as foreign_data, legalities, cards_foreign_texts_by_uuid, cards_color_identity_exploded, or any view marked as RANK/RESHAPE/SEL that expands to multiple rows per uuid without re-aggregation — doing so will multiply rows and therefore duplicate foreign_count and legalities_count unless you re-aggregate after the join. | If you must combine with a one-to-many sibling (e.g., card_rulings_latest, cards_foreign_texts_by_uuid), either: |   - aggregate the one-to-many side to one row per uuid before joining (e.g., MAX, COUNT, ARRAY_AGG then join), or |   - join first and then re-aggregate at the desired grain (e.g., GROUP BY uuid SUM(foreign_count) is not appropriate because foreign_count is already per-uuid; instead, SELECT uuid, MAX(foreign_count) ...). | Planner note: because foreign_count and legalities_count are pre-aggregated at the uuid grain, composition planners should treat them as atomic metrics at that grain. views.name: cards_power_status_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  cbp.id AS id,
  cbp.uuid AS uuid,
  cbp.name AS name,
  cbp.power AS power,
  CASE
    WHEN cbp.power IS NULL THEN 'NULL'
    WHEN trim(cbp.power) = '' THEN 'NULL'
    WHEN cbp.power = '*' THEN 'placeholder'
    WHEN cbp.power LIKE '%*%' THEN 'placeholder'
    WHEN cbp.power GLOB '[0-9]*' THEN 'concrete'
    WHEN cbp.power GLOB '[0-9]*/*' THEN 'concrete'
    WHEN cbp.power GLOB '*[0-9]*' THEN 'placeholder'
    ELSE
      -- treat any value that doesn't look like a numeric as placeholder
      CASE
        WHEN replace(replace(replace(cbp.power, '-', ''), '+', ''), '/', '') GLOB '*[0-9]*' THEN 'concrete'
        ELSE 'placeholder'
      END
  END AS power_status
FROM cards_base_projection cbp

This is the view grain (one row per id). | uuid: card UUID (derived from cards_base_projection.uuid). Unique identifier useful for joins keyed by uuid. | name: card name string (derived from cards_base_projection.name). | power: raw power text as stored (derived from cards_base_projection.power). | power_status: derived classification string computed from cards_base_projection.power with rules that treat NULL/empty as 'NULL', values containing '*' or non-numeric patterns as 'placeholder', and numeric-looking values (including those with slashes or leading/trailing signs) as 'concrete'.
params.metric:
power_status = CASE
  WHEN cards_base_projection.power IS NULL THEN 'NULL'
  WHEN trim(cards_base_projection.power) = '' THEN 'NULL'
  WHEN cards_base_projection.power = '*' THEN 'placeholder'
  WHEN cards_base_projection.power LIKE '%*%' THEN 'placeholder'
  WHEN cards_base_projection.power GLOB '[0-9]*' THEN 'concrete'
  WHEN cards_base_projection.power GLOB '[0-9]*/*' THEN 'concrete'
  WHEN cards_base_projection.power GLOB '*[0-9]*' THEN 'placeholder'
  ELSE
    CASE
      WHEN replace(replace(replace(cards_base_projection.power, '-', ''), '+', ''), '/', '') GLOB '*[0-9]*' THEN 'concrete'
      ELSE 'placeholder'
    END
END

Only safe if the target view/table is one-row-per-card (not one-to-many). views.name: cards_rowlevel
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  uuid,
  CAST(isTextless AS INTEGER) AS isTextless,
  layout
FROM cards

params.description: One-row-per-card identifiers and simple attributes (uuid, textless flag, layout) useful as a stable base for card-level joins and filters.
params.when_to_use: Fetch card identifiers and basic attributes for a single card or set of cards by id or uuid. | Serve as the card-level driving table when composing queries that add one-to-one or many-to-one card attributes (e.g., set info, current legality, translations) without changing cardinality. | Filter or join on the textless status or layout before aggregating or joining to related one-to-many datasets.
params.output_schema: id: internal numeric primary id for the card (derived from cards.id) | uuid: canonical card UUID (derived from cards.uuid) | isTextless: integer cast of cards.isTextless (0/1) indicating whether the card has no text; derived from CAST(cards.isTextless AS INTEGER) | layout: layout string for the card (derived from cards.layout)
params.metric: isTextless = CAST(cards.isTextless AS INTEGER)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to cards_with_set_info ON cards_rowlevel.id = cards_with_set_info.id — safe because cards_rowlevel is one-row-per-card (grain = id) and cards_with_set_info is a one-row-per-card enrichment (no multiplication of rows). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to cards_base_projection ON cards_rowlevel.id = cards_base_projection.id — safe because cards_base_projection projects base card columns at the same card id grain. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to card_legalities_current ON cards_rowlevel.id = card_legalities_current.card_id — safe when card_legalities_current is one-row-per-card (current legality per card); verify the sibling view's grain before joining. | UNSAFE without aggregation: do NOT join directly to one-to-many views/tables such as cards_foreign_latest_per_language, card_rulings_latest, cards_foreign_texts_by_uuid, cards_color_identity_exploded, cards_edhrec_rank_running, or set_translations_per_language if those siblings produce multiple rows per card — joining them directly will multiply cards_rowlevel rows and thus duplicate any measures derived at card grain. Instead, either: | - pre-aggregate the one-to-many side to one row per cards.id (e.g., group by card id and aggregate fields), or | - join using lateral/array aggregates to keep one row per card, or | - join to a sibling view that is explicitly one-row-per-card (e.g., cards_with_set_info) that already collapsed the many-side. | When composing metrics: any aggregate you compute on top of cards_rowlevel (e.g., COUNT(id), SUM(isTextless)) is correct at card grain. If you join a many-side without re-aggregation, those aggregates will be inflated by the multiplicity introduced by the join.

SELECT
  id,
  code,
  mcmName,
  releaseDate,
  name,
  type
FROM sets

params.description: Provides the canonical list of card sets (one row per set) including identifiers, display names, release date, and type.
params.when_to_use: Look up set metadata by set id or set code (e.g., name, release date, mcmName, type). | Filter or join card-level data to set-level attributes while preserving one-row-per-set semantics. | Compose higher-level aggregations or reports grouped by set (for counts, averages, ranks) using the set identifier or code as the grouping key.
params.output_schema: id: unique internal set identifier — comes from sets.id | code: short set code (e.g., 'M21') — comes from sets.code | mcmName: Market/third-party name variant for the set — comes from sets.mcmName | releaseDate: official set release date (date or timestamp) — comes from sets.releaseDate | name: canonical set display name — comes from sets.name | type: set classification/type (e.g., core, expansion, promo) — comes from sets.type
params.grounded_columns: sets.id | sets.code | sets.mcmName | sets.releaseDate | sets.name | sets.type
params.metric: No derived aggregates are produced by this view; all output columns are direct projections of base table columns. | Examples of metrics you can compute on top of this view (not defined here): |   card_count_per_set = COUNT(cards_base_projection.uuid) GROUP BY sets.id (must join cards and aggregate) |   average_edhrec_rank_per_set = AVG(cards_edhrec_rank_running.edhrec_rank) GROUP BY sets.id (requires joining and aggregating)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to cards_with_set (or cards_with_set_info / cards_base_projection) on sets.id = cards_with_set.set_id — NOT safe to join without aggregation if you intend to preserve one-row-per-set, because those card-level tables are one-to-many (one set -> many cards). To keep set measures unduplicated, either aggregate card measures to set first (e.g., GROUP BY sets.id) or use an EXISTS/IN or windowed deduplication. | Safe joins (will not duplicate set rows if you need one-row-per-set): |   - join to set_translations_per_language on sets.id = set_translations_per_language.set_id when expecting translations as additional attributes but only if you constrain to one language or aggregate translations per set; otherwise translations are one-to-many and will multiply rows. |   - join to any dimension that is one-to-one with sets.id or sets.code (for example, a hypothetical sets_metadata table keyed 1:1 by sets.id). | Unsafe joins (one-to-many, will multiply set rows unless you re-aggregate or deduplicate): |   - cards_base_projection, cards_with_set, cards_with_set_info, cards_color_identity_exploded, cards_foreign_latest_per_language, card_rulings_latest, cards_foreign_texts_by_uuid, cards_edhrec_rank_running, card_legalities_current, cards_cardkingdom_foil_absence_flag, legalities_by_card — these are card- or language- or ruling-level sources (one set -> many rows). If you join them directly to this sets view, you must either: |       * aggregate the child table to one row per sets.id before joining (e.g., SUM/COUNT/AVG GROUP BY set_id), or |       * join and then GROUP BY sets.id (re-aggregate) to avoid duplicating set-level measures, or |       * join using lateral or subqueries that return a single scalar value per set (e.g., latest rank, count, boolean flag). | Examples of safe composition patterns: |   - To get card counts per set: SELECT s.*, c.card_count FROM sets_core_71 s LEFT JOIN (SELECT set_id, COUNT(*) AS card_count FROM cards_base_projection GROUP BY set_id) c ON s.id = c.set_id |   - To attach a latest per-set metric already computed as one row per set (e.g., a pre-aggregated cards_edhrec_rank_running per set): join on sets.id = preagg.set_id — safe because preagg is one-row-per-set. | Notes: |   - Keys available for joins: sets.id (primary) and sets.code. Use the appropriate key that matches the child table's foreign key (commonly set_id or set_code). |   - This view does not contain measures (sums, counts) itself, so duplication concerns arise when enriching it with one-to-many child data; follow the guidance above to preserve correctness.

views.name: set_translations_by_set
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  set_translations.id AS "set_translations.id",
  set_translations.setCode AS "set_translations.setCode",
  set_translations.language AS "set_translations.language",
  set_translations.translation AS "set_translations.translation",
  sets.id AS "sets.id as set_id",
  sets.code AS "sets.code as set_code",
  sets.mcmName AS "sets.mcmName",
  sets.name AS "sets.name as set_name"
FROM set_translations
LEFT JOIN sets
  ON set_translations.setCode = sets.code

params.description: Provides one row per set_translation (a translation of a set name) with joined set metadata from sets.
params.when_to_use: Find the translated name of a set in a particular language and include canonical set attributes (id, code, mcmName, name). | Filter or aggregate translations by language or set code when building reports about set localization. | Compose into queries that need set translation rows enriched with the corresponding set record without changing cardinality (one row per set_translation).
params.output_schema: set_translations.id: primary key of the set_translations row (derived from set_translations.id). | set_translations.setCode: the set code on the translation row (derived from set_translations.setCode). | set_translations.language: ISO or site language code for this translation (derived from set_translations.language). | set_translations.translation: the translated text for the set name (derived from set_translations.translation). | sets.id as set_id: numeric primary key of the referenced sets row (derived from sets.id). | sets.code as set_code: canonical set code from sets (derived from sets.code). | sets.mcmName: mcmName field from sets, often an external marketplace name (derived from sets.mcmName). | sets.name as set_name: canonical name of the set in the base language (derived from sets.name).
params.grounded_columns: set_translations.id | set_translations.setCode | set_translations.language | set_translations.translation | sets.id | sets.code | sets.mcmName | sets.name
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension tables keyed by set_code or sets.id preserving one-row-per-set_translation: |   - Safe: join to sets on set_code / sets.code (already done in this view). This view is one-row-per set_translations.id, and sets is at-most-one row per sets.code, so joining sets does not duplicate measures. |   - Safe: join to any one-to-one or many-to-one dimension keyed by sets.id or sets.code (for example, a sets_metadata dimension keyed by sets.id) because those joins will not increase row multiplicity relative to set_translations. |   - Do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables or views keyed by sets.id or sets.code (for example, cards_with_set which is one-to-many from sets -> cards, or any card-level view) without first aggregating that one-to-many side back to sets or set_translations.id. Such joins will multiply rows (each set_translation would be duplicated for every matching card) and thus would duplicate counts/measures unless the downstream query re-aggregates. |   - If you need card-level information with set translations, either: (a) aggregate card-level measures up to sets.code or sets.id before joining to this view, or (b) join this view to a card-level dataset and then GROUP BY set_translations.id (or set_translations.setCode + set_translations.language) to re-establish the intended grain. |   - When composing: prefer joining on set_translations.setCode = other.set_code OR sets.id = other.set_id depending on which side has a unique key. Use sets.code/sets.id when the other dataset is keyed to sets; use set_translations.setCode when keyed to translation-side code.

params.output_schema: foreign_data.id: Unique identifier for this foreign_data row; sourced from foreign_data.id | foreign_data.uuid: The card's canonical uuid associated with this translation; sourced from foreign_data.uuid | foreign_data.language: Language code/identifier for this translation (e.g., 'en', 'jp'); sourced from foreign_data.language | foreign_data.name: Translated name field for the card in this language; sourced from foreign_data.name | foreign_data.text: Translated oracle/text content (rules text) for the card in this language; sourced from foreign_data.text | foreign_data.flavorText: Translated flavor text for the card in this language; sourced from foreign_data.flavorText

params.metric: No aggregated metrics are defined in this view. All output columns are direct projections from base columns. | Derived_col = <none>

If the target view is one-to-many (e.g., multiple set printings per uuid), that will multiply translation rows unless you pre-aggregate or restrict the set-side to one row per uuid. | Do NOT blindly join to one-to-many tables/views such as card_rulings_latest, cards_foreign_texts_by_uuid, cards_color_identity_exploded, cards_edhrec_rank_running, cards_with_set (if it has multiple printings per uuid), or card_legalities_current without ensuring you join on keys that preserve uniqueness or you re-aggregate after the join — such joins can duplicate translation rows because they introduce multiple rows per foreign_data.id. | If you need to combine with one-to-many siblings (for example, rulings or multiple set printings), either: |   - aggregate the one-to-many side to one row per foreign_data.uuid (or per foreign_data.id) before joining, or |   - join first to a deduplicated / nearest-per-uuid view such as card_foreign_latest_per_language (if applicable) or a view that enforces one-row-per-uuid, or |   - join on both uuid and an additional key that enforces a single match (e.g., language + uuid when the other side is scoped the same way). | Example safe composition patterns: |   - foreign translations + card base: JOIN card_translations_by_uuid ON card_translations_by_uuid.foreign_data.uuid = cards_base_projection.uuid (returns one translation row per foreign_data.id, not duplicated) |   - translations aggregated by language: SELECT foreign_data.language, COUNT(*) FROM card_translations_by_uuid GROUP BY foreign_data.language (aggregation done after projection) | Examples of unsafe patterns without re-aggregation/deduplication: |   - card_translations_by_uuid JOIN card_rulings_latest ON uuid = uuid  -- rulings are one-to-many and will multiply translation rows |   - card_translations_by_uuid JOIN cards_with_set (if that view contains multiple rows per uuid for different printings) ON uuid = uuid  -- will multiply translation rows
